contract_findings: The pass holds P5 vocabulary only: a decisive outer contour, major clothing and hair breaks, hand and boot silhouettes taken from verified P4 blocks, major prop topology, and replayable construction retirement.
No tone rendering, knit or denim texture, micro folds, seams, fingers, boot panel details, facial features or shading was introduced.
Retirement was performed with soft_lift on named strokes, so it stays replayable; nothing was raster-erased.
corrections: Stated the full P5 contour, then retired 69 construction strokes with replayable soft_lift at stage-appropriate strengths.
drawing_findings: whole_silhouette: the figure and the slung rifle read immediately from silhouette; head-to-body proportion, shoulder span, waist, leg spread and both landings remain credible against the subject, and no retired construction is dark enough to compete with the contour.
whole_silhouette: the dominant P1 gesture survives faintly and still explains the weight path, which is the one piece of construction the reference asks to keep.

prop_topology: the prop is not two generic rails. Suppressor-to-barrel step, scope, receiver widening and buttstock cutout are all readable, and the prop keeps its own contour ownership across the torso.

handoff_prop_garment: a real defect. Contour-contact evidence gives a minimum sampled distance of 7 pixels at canvas (151,214) with a 36 degree tangent angle, and the two strokes cross near canvas y=225 while both are drawn at full outer-contour weight. The result reads as an X of two equal contours instead of an ownership handoff.

handoff_hair_shoulder: contour-contact evidence gives 1.4 pixels minimum distance on the image-right at an 87 degree angle and 6.3 pixels on the image-left at 85 degrees. The near-perpendicular meeting stops them welding, but the hair edge simply stops at the shoulder instead of continuing inside the garment as an overlap contour, so the hair does not read as resting on the shoulder.
Fresh residual sweep: no cleanup changed verified structure, and no major clothing or hair envelope was omitted.
exemplar_findings: The bundled P5 exemplar carries a KNOWN AUDIT FAILURE for exceeding the clean-block-in ceiling with shading, micro folds and texture; only its silhouette-first ordering was used and none of its rendering was imitated.

The subject's rifle owns the outer left silhouette above roughly canvas y=225 and the jacket owns it below, so the two edges genuinely cross rather than merge.
The subject's bob tips rest on top of both shoulders, so the hair edge continues inside the garment after the garment takes the outer silhouette.
The subject's prop is readable only through its width changes, its scope and the large cutout in the skeleton buttstock.
